topic: A profile full of old films
title_jp: {古い|ふるい}{映画|えいが}が{好きな|すきな}{人|ひと}
context: Wednesday: the rubbish went out on time and {恵子|けいこ}さん is back from {長野市|ながのし}. That night, under the kotatsu, アルちゃん finally tries the dating app {健太|けんた} suggested and finds the profile of レン, 26, a designer who loves old films.
scene: Wednesday night under the kotatsu. You finally open the dating app {健太|けんた} suggested, and one profile is all about old films.

phrases.jp: {映画|えいが}の{趣味|しゅみ|taste, hobby|4}が{合いそう|あいそう|to match, suit|4}ですね。
phrases.en: Looks like we have the same taste in films.
phrases.note: {趣味|しゅみ}が{合|あ}う = share tastes. A classic, safe first message on dating apps.

phrases.jp: {僕|ぼく}も{人見知り|ひとみしり|shy with strangers|3}だけど、{慣れたら|なれたら|to get used to|4}よくしゃべるよ。
phrases.en: I'm shy with new people too, but once I'm used to you I talk a lot.
phrases.note: Japanese people describe themselves this way all the time; it's a friendly warning, not a flaw.

phrases.jp: えー、そんなわけないじゃん！
phrases.note: わけがない with が dropped, plus じゃん. The instant reply to something absurd.

phrases.jp: {初めて|はじめて}のメッセージ、{緊張|きんちょう|being nervous|4}しないわけがないよ。
phrases.en: A first message? Of course I'm nervous.
phrases.note: Double negative = strong yes: しないわけがない ≈ {絶対|ぜったい}する.

phrases.jp: {返信|へんしん|reply (to a message)|3}が{遅くなって|おそくなって|to be late, slow|4}すみません。
phrases.note: The standard opener on LINE or email. Casual: {返信|へんしん}{遅|おそ}くなってごめん！

dialogue_setting: A profile on a dating app (マッチングアプリ), read on アルちゃん's phone late at night.
text_title: レン（26）・{長野市|ながのし}

dialogue.speaker: About me
dialogue.jp: はじめまして。{長野市|ながのし}でデザイナーをしています。{東京|とうきょう}の{大学|だいがく}を{出て|でて}、{地元|じもと|hometown, local area|3}に{戻りました|もどりました|to return|4}。
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you. I'm a designer in {長野市|ながのし}. I went to university in Tokyo, then came back to my hometown.

dialogue.speaker: Hobbies
dialogue.jp: {趣味|しゅみ|hobby|4}は{古い|ふるい}{映画|えいが}と{フィルムカメラ||film camera|2}。{休み|やすみ}の{日|ひ}は{街|まち}の{小さな|ちいさな}{映画館|えいがかん|cinema|4}に{通って|かよって|to go regularly|4}います。
dialogue.en: My hobbies are old films and film cameras. On my days off I go to a small cinema in town.

dialogue.speaker: Favourite film
dialogue.jp: {一番|いちばん}は{小津安二郎|おづやすじろう}の『{東京物語|とうきょうものがたり}』。{静か|しずか}だけど、{家族|かぞく}の{会話|かいわ|conversation|4}が{リアル||realistic|3}な{作品|さくひん|work (of art)|3}です。
dialogue.en: My favourite is {小津安二郎|おづやすじろう}'s 'Tokyo Story'. It's quiet, but the family's conversations feel so real.

dialogue.speaker: Personality
dialogue.jp: {普段|ふだん|usually, normally|4}は{人見知り|ひとみしり|shy with strangers|3}ですが、{映画|えいが}の{話|はなし}になると{熱く|あつく|passionate, heated|3}なります。
dialogue.en: I'm usually shy with new people, but when films come up I get passionate.

dialogue.speaker: Question
dialogue.jp: {白黒|しろくろ|black and white|3}{映画|えいが}は{退屈|たいくつ|boring|3}？そんなわけがない！{一度|いちど}{見て|みて}みてください。
dialogue.en: Black-and-white films are boring? No way! Try watching one.

dialogue.speaker: Mornings
dialogue.jp: コーヒーは{毎朝|まいあさ}{自分|じぶん}で{淹れます|いれます|to brew (coffee, tea)|3}。コーヒーなしで{朝|あさ}が{始まる|はじまる}わけがないので。
dialogue.en: I make my own coffee every morning. There's no way a morning can start without it.

dialogue.speaker: Looking for
dialogue.jp: {一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見たり|みたり}、{山|やま}を{歩いたり|あるいたり}できる{人|ひと}に{出会えたら|であえたら|to meet (by chance)|3}{嬉しい|うれしい}です。
dialogue.en: I'd be happy to meet someone to watch films and walk in the mountains with.

dialogue.speaker: Note
dialogue.jp: ※{返信|へんしん|reply (to a message)|3}が{遅い|おそい}ことがあります。ごめんなさい！
dialogue.en: ※ Sometimes I'm slow to reply. Sorry!

listening.intro: Later that night you match, and レン sends his first message. Type what he writes.

lines.jp: はじめまして！スペインの{映画|えいが}、{僕|ぼく}も{好き|すき}です。
lines.en: Nice to meet you! I like Spanish films too.

grammar.form: verb: plain form + わけがない ({始|はじ}まるわけがない, {知|し}らないわけがない) · い-adj: + わけがない ({高|たか}いわけがない) · な-adj: + な + わけがない ({退屈|たいくつ}なわけがない) · noun: + の / な + わけがない ({嘘|うそ}のわけがない) · spoken: わけない (そんなわけないじゃん)
grammar.explanation: A strong denial based on your own reasoning: 'there's no way'. In speech が drops: そんなわけない！ is the classic reply to an absurd idea. Don't confuse it with わけではない ('it's not that…'), which only softens; わけがない flatly rules something out.
mark: 覚えているわけがない

examples.jp: あの{店|みせ}のラーメンがまずいわけがないよ。いつも{行列|ぎょうれつ|queue|3}だもん。
examples.en: There's no way that shop's ramen is bad. There's always a queue.

examples.jp: {一度|いちど}{会った|あった}だけの{人|ひと}の{名前|なまえ}を、{覚えて|おぼえて}いるわけがない。
examples.en: There's no way I'd remember the name of someone I met just once.

examples.jp: こんなに{静か|しずか}な{町|まち}が{危険|きけん|dangerous|3}なわけがない。
examples.en: A town this quiet can't possibly be dangerous.

quiz.question: {彼|かれ}は{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しているから、{下手|へた|bad at|4}＿＿。
quiz.en: He practises every day, so there's no way he's bad at it.
quiz.explain: 下手 is a な-adjective, so it takes な before わけがない, never だ.

quiz_more.question: あの{二人|ふたり}が{付き合って|つきあって|to date|3}る？そんな＿＿じゃん！
quiz_more.en: Those two are dating? No way!
quiz_more.explain: そんなわけない(じゃん) = 'no way!', with が dropped in speech. わけだ and はずだ say it IS so.

quiz_more.question: {映画|えいが}が{嫌い|きらい}な＿＿。{今日|きょう}は{疲れて|つかれて}いるだけ。
quiz_more.en: It's not that I dislike films. I'm just tired today.
quiz_more.explain: Softening a misunderstanding ('it's not that…') needs わけではない; わけがない would flatly deny it.

kanji.where: The heading over the 'About me' part of every dating-app and social-media profile, and on school and job forms.
kanji.breakdown: {自己紹介|じこしょうかい}: 自己 oneself + 紹介 introduction → 'introducing yourself'.
kanji.related: {紹介|しょうかい}する = to introduce; {自己|じこ}PR = selling yourself on a job form.

tip.title: Profiles without faces
tip.body: On Japanese dating apps (マチアプ for short) many people show a coffee cup, a pet or a mountain instead of their face, to stay discreet in a small town. Every app must check your age with an ID ({年齢確認|ねんれいかくにん}) by law, so expect to upload one before you can message.

challenge.hint: な-adjective + な + わけがない
challenge.prompt: In his profile レン asks 「{白黒|しろくろ|black and white|3}{映画|えいが}は{退屈|たいくつ|boring|3}？」 You write him a first message: there's no way they're boring, and you love 『{東京物語|とうきょうものがたり}』 too. One part is wrong.

parts.jp: {白黒|しろくろ}{映画|えいが}が

parts.why: {退屈|たいくつ} is a な-adjective: it keeps な before わけ ({退屈|たいくつ}なわけがない), never だ.

parts.jp: 『{東京物語|とうきょうものがたり}』、{僕|ぼく}も{大好き|だいすき}です！

challenge.model_answer: {白黒|しろくろ|black and white|3}{映画|えいが}が{退屈|たいくつ|boring|3}なわけがないですよ。『{東京物語|とうきょうものがたり}』、{僕|ぼく}も{大好き|だいすき}です！
challenge.explanation: {退屈|たいくつ} is a な-adjective, so it keeps な before わけがない. Adding ですよ keeps the strong 'no way' polite and friendly, right for a first message to someone you haven't met. {僕|ぼく}も{大好き|だいすき} shows you share his taste.

vocab.note: 地 land + 元 origin. {地元|じもと}の{人|ひと} = the locals.
{趣味|しゅみ}が{合|あ}う = to share tastes. {趣味|しゅみ}が{悪|わる}い = bad taste.
映画 film + 館 building, as in {図書館|としょかん} and {美術館|びじゅつかん}.
作る make + 品 article. Used for films, novels, paintings, a child's drawing.
Your normal state, as opposed to now. {普段着|ふだんぎ} = everyday clothes.
人 people + {見知|みし}る know by sight. {人見知|ひとみし}りする = to be shy at first.
{熱|あつ}いお{茶|ちゃ}; {熱|あつ}くなる = get fired up. Hot weather is {暑|あつ}い.
Japanese says white first. {白黒|しろくろ}つける = settle who's right.
な-adjective: {退屈|たいくつ}な{映画|えいが}. {退屈|たいくつ}する = to be bored.
{返|へん} return + {信|しん} message. {返信|へんしん}が{遅|おそ}い = slow to reply.

kanji_study.kun: しりぞ(く)・しりぞ(ける)
kanji_study.parts: ⻌ road radical (moving) + 艮 a person turning to look back → walking away backwards: retreat, withdraw. 退屈 is a mind that has withdrawn: bored.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 追 (chase): both sit on ⻌, but 退 has 艮 on top, 追 has 𠂤.

kanji_study.parts: 埶 a person holding up a plant + 灬 fire radical (four dots) underneath → fire burning under it: heat, fever, passion.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 勢 (force): same top, but 勢 has 力 power below, 熱 has the fire dots 灬.

extras.title: Describing someone's personality
extras.title_jp: {性格|せいかく}の{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: Words you'll see in every profile, and hear when friends ask 'what's he like?'.

items.jp: {明るくて|あかるくて}、よく{笑う|わらう}{人|ひと}です。
items.en: He's cheerful and laughs a lot.
items.note: {明|あか}るい = bright, cheerful: the top compliment.

items.jp: {真面目|まじめ|serious, earnest|4}だけど、{面白い|おもしろい}ところもある。
items.en: He's serious, but he has a funny side too.
items.note: {真面目|まじめ} is a compliment in Japan, not 'boring'.

items.jp: {落ち着いて|おちついて|to be calm|4}いて、{話しやすい|はなしやすい}。
items.en: He's calm and easy to talk to.
items.note: 〜やすい = easy to. A very common way to praise someone.

items.jp: ちょっと{天然|てんねん|airheaded, naturally ditzy|3}なところがかわいい。
items.en: He's a bit of a space cadet, and it's cute.
items.note: {天然|てんねん} = 'natural': slang for sweetly clueless.

extras.title: Talking about films
extras.intro: Four words for a night at the cinema.

items.jp: {字幕|じまく|subtitles|3}と{吹き替え|ふきかえ|dubbing|3}、どっちが{好き|すき}？
items.en: Subtitles or dubbing, which do you prefer?
items.note: Cinemas list both: {字幕版|じまくばん} / {吹替版|ふきかえばん}.

items.jp: {邦画|ほうが|Japanese film|2}より{洋画|ようが|Western film|2}をよく{見る|みる}。
items.en: I watch more foreign films than Japanese ones.
items.note: {邦画|ほうが} = Japanese films, {洋画|ようが} = Western ones.

items.jp: ちょっと{待って|まって}、ネタバレしないで！
items.note: ネタバレ = spoiler (ネタ material + バレる be revealed).
